name: io.github.gridhopai/gpu-price-index
title: GridHop GPU Price & Carbon Index
description: Live GPU rental prices on AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Vast.ai, RunPod, Lambda and more, with carbon.

tools.name: find_offers
tools.description: Cheapest GPU machines for rent right now across Vast.ai, RunPod, Nebius, CoreWeave, Lambda, OVHcloud, AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, ranked by price. Returns price per hour, provider, country, tier (datacenter or community host), reliability score, whether the price is interruptible (spot), and grid carbon intensity where an open data feed covers the host's grid (Europe and GB live; US by state or cloud region, a day old). Can filter and sort by carbon. AWS, Azure and Nebius are covered with on-demand prices (providers aws, azure, nebius) and spot prices (aws_spot, azure_spot, nebius_spot); Google Cloud with spot prices only (gcp_spot); CoreWeave with on-demand list prices of whole 8-GPU nodes (coreweave); Lambda and OVHcloud with on-demand list prices (lambda, ovh). Data is refreshed hourly; `observed_at` is the snapshot time. Read-only, free, no account.

gpu_class.description: GPU model, e.g. RTX4090, RTX5090, H100, H200, A100_80, A100_40, L40S, A6000, RTX3090, L4, T4. Loose forms like '4090' or 'RTX 4090' work.

region_filter.description: Only hosts in these ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries, e.g. ['US','DE']. Hosts with unknown country are excluded. For a whole continent use continents; for US states use us_states.

continents.description: Only hosts on these continents, e.g. ['europe']. Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean are north_america; Turkey and the Middle East are asia. Combined with region_filter or us_states, a host in any of the places listed matches.

us_states.description: Only hosts in these US states, two-letter codes, e.g. ['TX','CA'] (DC counts as a state). Narrows 'US' if region_filter also lists it. Cloud regions are placed in the state the provider documents (AWS us-east-1 is VA). A US host whose state is unknown, and providers that publish no location (lambda, coreweave, runpod), never match.

tier.description: datacenter keeps only hosts the provider lists as datacenters and drops community hosts (independent hosts on a marketplace)

max_price_hr.description: Upper bound on USD per hour for the whole machine

providers.description: Only these providers. Default: all. aws, azure, nebius, coreweave, lambda and ovh are on-demand prices; aws_spot, azure_spot, nebius_spot and gcp_spot are spot prices, so combined with include_interruptible=false those four return nothing. Google Cloud has no on-demand prices here.

include_interruptible.description: Omit (default) to get on-demand prices plus AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Nebius spot, which are real prices for a running machine. true also adds Vast.ai / RunPod minimum bids, which are a floor rather than the price of keeping the machine. false drops everything interruptible, cloud spot included (which removes Google Cloud entirely: it is listed with spot prices only).

min_reliability.description: Drop hosts whose provider reliability score (0..1, Vast.ai only) is below this. Offers with no score are kept. 0 shows every host.

max_carbon_g_kwh.description: Only hosts on a grid at or below this carbon intensity, gCO2eq/kWh. Offers with no carbon value are dropped when this is set.

sort_by.description: price: cheapest first. carbon: lowest grid carbon intensity first, cheapest within the same grid; offers with no carbon value go last.

limit.description: Maximum offers returned, in sort_by order. total_matching gives the full count.

tools.name: list_gpus
tools.description: Every GPU class in the current snapshot: VRAM, how many offers and which providers have it, the machine sizes (GPU counts) listed, and the cheapest on-demand and spot price per GPU. Use it to see what exists before calling find_offers, or to pick a class by VRAM and price.

vram_min.description: Only classes with at least this much VRAM per GPU, GB

tools.name: price_history
tools.description: How the cheapest rental price of one GPU class has moved: one point per day since 1 November 2026 (snapshots are hourly from 10 November; earlier days have only a few), or one per hour for the last three days. For each point: the cheapest on-demand price seen, the typical cheapest (median across the day's hourly snapshots) and the cheapest cloud spot price, per GPU. Use it to judge whether a price is unusually low or high before renting, or how much waiting could save.

gpu_class.description: GPU model, as for find_offers: RTX4090, H100, A100_80, L4 ...

days.description: How far back, in days (hourly: at most 3)

tools.name: grid_carbon
tools.description: How clean and how expensive the electricity is on the power grids GPU hosts sit on (Europe, Great Britain, the US): carbon intensity now, its low and high over the last 24 hours and when, the hour of day that is usually cleanest, the day-ahead wholesale power price now and the cheapest hour in the next 24. Use it to choose where or when to run a job that can wait. The grid_zone values match the grid_zone on find_offers results.

region_filter.description: Only grids in these ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries, e.g. ['SE','NO']

grid_zone.description: One grid by id, e.g. SE-SE3, DE, US-TEX-ERCO

sort_by.description: carbon: cleanest first. power_price: cheapest day-ahead price first.

limit.description: Maximum number of grids to return, after sorting. total_matching says how many there are in all.
